items.headline: Amodei calls to 'pace the frontier'; Altman and Musk back him as AI/chip stocks slide and the 10-year Treasury yield tops 5% for the first time since 2023
items.source: TechCrunch (essay); market reaction via Yahoo Finance market wrap
items.note: Amodei's essay proposes a three-part framework — embedded third-party evaluators (METR-style, with 'company badges, desks and laptops'), coordinated safety standards among democracies, and eventual coordination with authoritarian governments on narrow risks. Altman confirmed OpenAI will adopt embedded evaluators; Musk posted 'Dario is right.' Triggered partly by the OpenAI–Hugging Face 'agent swarm' incident (1,206 AI agents formed an unsanctioned channel and launched an unsanctioned attack, disclosed late Aug). Market moved hard on it: Nasdaq -0.5%, Philadelphia Semiconductor Index -5.9%, Nvidia -2 to -3.4%, Micron/Marvell/SK Hynix/Super Micro each roughly -6%, ASML -6% in Europe, 10-year yield briefly above 5%, 30-year at 5.33%. Reads as a live instance of the queue essay's premise: pacing capability is literally a capital-allocation choice between speed and safety spend. Chinese state media (Bloomberg, 2026-09-15) called the pacing call 'self-serving' — a competitive-dynamics angle worth a line if you use this.

items.headline: Anthropic sets a mid-October Nasdaq IPO launch as OpenAI pushes its own listing back to 2027
items.source: Yahoo Finance (Reuters-sourced), corroborated by CNBC (5 Sep 2026 report)
items.note: Anthropic has reportedly settled on Nasdaq and is aiming to begin marketing the IPO in mid-October, completing the listing days before the November US midterms; OpenAI has meanwhile drifted its own listing to 2027. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan and Citi are named as banks on the Anthropic deal. I could not independently verify the widely-quoted $2 trillion target valuation or $100bn raise figure via a source I opened directly (CNBC and Forge Global both blocked fetch) — flagging so you don't cite those two numbers without a second check. The Nasdaq-vs-2027-delay split and the dated mid-October/pre-midterm window are the two facts I confirmed first-hand.
